items.q: What does Arcolano's golf analogy compare the AI model to?
items.a: The **clubs**: better clubs help a bit, but the **golfer and the course** matter far more.

items.q: What happened to output when Cursor pushed engineers onto a different model?
items.a: **Nothing measurable**: merged PRs per engineer **didn't change**.

items.q: How much of the variation in PR throughput does the tool/model explain?
items.a: **Under 1%**; switching models or harnesses is **statistically a nothingburger**.

items.q: How much did heavy skill use (30+ runs a week) raise output?
items.a: About **30%**, yet almost **half of engineer-weeks had no skill use**.

items.q: What does 10x more tokens buy, from median to top 10%?
items.a: Roughly **2x output**: more tokens help, with **diminishing returns**.

items.q: How much does where you work matter at equal AI spend?
items.a: A **2x spread** between top and bottom companies, from **codebase, review process and culture**.

items.q: What's the biggest factor in AI-era engineering output?
items.a: **The individual** engineer, about **three quarters** of the model, with a 3.5x spread.

items.q: Has AI reshuffled who the best engineers are?
items.a: No: **your best engineers before AI are still your best engineers**.

items.q: What should leaders focus on instead of model choice?
items.a: **People, skills adoption and the environment**: unlike golf, **you can change the course**.
